fields.population: Minas Gerais municipalities and their sanitation service providers, 2010-2019 (data for 2014-2015 absent)
fields.sample_size: 853 municipalities x 10 years = 8,530 panel rows; final model 2,589 municipality-year observations (unbalanced; the policy variable PPSB is missing in 4,736 of 8,530 rows and entirely for 2014 and 2015)
fields.effect_measure: fixed-effects binomial logistic regression (panel); coefficients in log-odds (Hausman test rejects random effects, chi2(9) = 40.24, p < 0.001)
fields.effect_estimate: Outcome: municipality has a basic-sanitation policy/plan (PPSB) in line with Law 11,445/2007 (SNIS). Institutional capacity gives mixed signs: operating revenue per capita (ln) -0.638 (SE 0.267, z -2.39, p = 0.017; OR about 0.53, derived 95% CI about 0.31-0.89) -- higher revenue, LOWER probability of a plan; total expenses per capita (ln) +0.624 (SE 0.267, p = 0.020; OR about 1.87, derived CI about 1.11-3.15); own employees per 10,000 -0.020 (SE 0.015, p = 0.177, not significant). Controls: Bolsa Familia -0.063 (p < 0.001), population aging +0.039 (p < 0.001), health expenditure (ln) +0.865 (p = 0.001); municipal revenue, GDP and urbanisation not significant. The authors call the capacity effect 'varied' and contrary to their hypothesis (H1: greater capacity, greater probability); they suggest revenue-rich providers lack an incentive to plan and that political will, not resources, may be the binding constraint. PPSB prevalence among reporting municipalities: 82% (2010), 19% (2011), 48% (2019), which the authors attribute to changing data reporting.
fields.adjusted_or_unadjusted: adjusted (fixed effects; revenue, GDP, Bolsa Familia, urbanisation, aging, health expenditure)
fields.covariates: municipal budget revenue (ln), GDP per capita (ln), Bolsa Familia per capita, urbanisation, aging index, health expenditure per capita (ln); municipality fixed effects
fields.model_type: fixed-effects binomial logistic regression on an unbalanced panel
fields.study_design: quantitative panel-data analysis of municipalities (observational; exposure is institutional capacity, not an intervention)
fields.section: Full text (urbe. Revista Brasileira de Gestao Urbana 17:e20240028): Abstract; Methodological procedures; Results and discussions (Tables 2-3); Final considerations
fields.exact_location: Abstract p1-2; Methodological procedures p5-7 (Table 1 variables; Hausman and endogeneity tests p7); Results p8-12 (Table 2 descriptives p10; Table 3 coefficients p11); Final considerations p13

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a fixed-effects logistic panel analysis of 853 Minas Gerais municipalities (2,589 model observations, 2010-2019), read in full text 2026-10-04. Municipal sanitation-plan adoption under Law 11,445/2007 is associated with higher service expenditure (OR about 1.9) but with LOWER operating revenue (OR about 0.5) and is unrelated to staff numbers; the authors conclude capacity matters but not in the expected direction. Heavy missing data (PPSB missing in 56% of rows); observational.

notes: CORRECTS the abstract-level extraction, which said weaker institutional capacity made adoption of the mandated plan systematically less likely; the full text shows mixed signs (revenue negative, expenses positive, staff not significant) and a final model of 2,589 observations, not 8,530. EFFECT-SIZE CANDIDATE (log-odds with SEs, Table 3): expenditure and revenue coefficients for the legal-compliance outcome; not added (human approval, see A13). TOOL MISFIT: ROBINS-I does not fit an observational panel regression of institutional capacity (no intervention); old Moderate rating left in place for the reclassification step (A11).
